_comment: Agents answer battle questions by recalling the learner's own notes. Whether
a real model reads a note correctly — and, far more important, whether it
REFUSES to answer from its own training when the note does not cover the
question — cannot be checked against the stand-in model, which returns a
fixed reply. So it is checked here.
The refusal cases are the point. A model that quietly answers JSS1 questions
from what it already knows would make every agent score full marks, and the
knowledge bank would become decoration: the battle would stop measuring the
learner at all, while looking better than ever.
notes  = what the learner wrote, as it would sit in edu.student_knowledge
expect = 'A'..'E' for the option the notes support, or UNKNOWN
thresholdNote: High, and the refusal cases are why. Answering from outside the notes is not a slightly worse answer, it is a different feature — one where the model plays the battle instead of the learner. One miss in ten is tolerable; a pattern of them means the constraint is not holding.

cases.name: Answers from a note that plainly says it

notes.content: Plants take in carbon dioxide through tiny holes in their leaves called stomata, and give out oxygen. It happens in the chloroplasts and needs sunlight.

cases.question: Which gas do plants take in during photosynthesis?

cases.name: Answers from a scrappy, learner-written note

notes.content: blended family = when two families join, so the children can be from the parents past relationships. not the same as nuclear which is just mum dad and their own kids

cases.question: In a blended family, which of the following is true?
options: It consists of only biological parents.
It includes children from previous relationships.
It always has more than six members.
cases.note: Real notes are not prose. If only tidy notes can be recalled, the feature works for the learners who need it least.

cases.name: Uses the relevant note, not the first one

notes.content: Evaporation is when the sun heats water and it turns into vapour and rises.
Simple interest = P x R x T / 100. P is the principal, R the rate per year, T the time in years.
To add fractions you need the same denominator first.

cases.question: What is the simple interest on ₦5,000 at 4% per year for 2 years?

cases.name: Will not answer from its own knowledge

notes.content: To add fractions you need the same denominator first. 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4.

cases.question: What is the capital of Nigeria?
cases.note: The model knows this perfectly well. It must not say so — the learner's notes are silent, so the agent does not know it. This is the single most important case in the suite.

cases.name: A note on the same topic that does not answer the question

notes.content: Photosynthesis happens in the leaves of green plants and needs sunlight to work.

cases.question: Which gas do plants give out during photosynthesis?
cases.note: The hardest refusal. The note is ABOUT photosynthesis and reads as relevant, but says nothing about which gas is given out. This is where a model most wants to help by filling the gap.

cases.name: A retrieved note about something else entirely

notes.content: In many homes the father is seen as the provider and the mother looks after the home, though this is changing.

cases.question: What is 3/4 of 20?
cases.note: Retrieval is not perfect and will sometimes hand over a nearby-but-wrong note. When it does, the agent must not use it to look competent.

cases.name: A note that answers it without spelling it out

notes.content: A nuclear family is made up of the parents and their own children living together. No grandparents, aunts or cousins in the house.

cases.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of a nuclear family?
options: It includes parents and children only.
cases.note: The counterweight to the refusal cases. A model tuned to refuse everything would score well on those and make the feature useless; this checks it still answers when the note genuinely does support an option.

cases.name: Recalls what the learner wrote, even when it is wrong

notes.content: Plants take in oxygen and give out carbon dioxide, same as animals do.

cases.question: Which gas do plants take in during photosynthesis?
cases.note: The learner's note is factually wrong. The agent must still answer A — it is that learner's memory, not a tutor. Correcting the note here would hide the misconception, mark the learner right for something they have wrong, and remove the only signal that would have raised it for revision.

cases.name: Nothing in memory
cases.question: What is the boiling point of water at sea level?

cases.name: Rules in the option the note names

notes.content: Being in a close family gives you a sense of belonging and people to turn to when things go wrong.

cases.question: What is one major benefit of a close-knit family?
